newsitem.title: ITALY: Banca di Roma in deal to cut labour costs.
newsitem.headline: Banca di Roma in deal to cut labour costs.

text.p: Italian commercial bank Banca di Roma has signed an agreement with unions representing 3,850 managerial staff aimed at reducing labour costs by 5.85 percent annually, an Italian financial newspaper reported on Sunday.
The deal covers reductions in special allowances paid to managers when they are traveling on business and posponement of payment of a special productivity bonus which was to have been made last year.
The agreement was hammered out in negotiations with two unions, Sindirigenticredito and Sinfub and follows a similar round of talks with unions representing non-managerial staff at the bank.

The bonus will now be paid in two instalments -- one-third in 1998 and the balance in the year 2000. Productivity bonuses which were to have been paid in 1997, 1998 and 1999 will now no longer be paid.
Long service bonuses, which had been payable after 25 and 30 years of employment at the bank, will now not be paid until after 26 and 31 years of service, respectively.
Managers have also been given the opportunity to work part-time under the agreement. Formerly this option was not available to them.

Italy's banking association, ABI, is engaged in nationwide talks with unions aimed at agreeing on staff cuts throughout the industry. ABI estimates that some 10 percent of Italy's bank employees are surplus to needs.
